Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Initial MAP and hosting considerations for POC

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed with Ben, Healix is ready to lock a short MAP so we can evaluate Redwood for our inference tier. Two strong constraints from our side: (1) we need data to remain in-region for EU traffic; (2) we require an option that satisfies our procurement team for a SOC2-backed provider (we will ask for artifacts).

High level asks:
- Can you outline Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private trade-offs specifically for our workload (100 qps peak, median seq len ~512)?
- A recommended eval plan (perf targets, ramp steps, canary criteria) and a close timeline to move from POC -> production in 8–10 weeks if things go well.

Ben is on copy for procurement details. We would like a one-page MAP and a short ops runbook attached.

Cheers,
Julia
Julia Park
VP Product, Healix Labs
julia.park@healixlabs.com

Attachments: none (will accept Redwood MAP + SOC artifacts via Drive link)

Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial MAP and hosting considerations for POC

Hi Julia — great to hear and thanks for the clear constraints.

Opening notes and proposed next steps (high level):
1) Quick recommendation: For Healix's target (100 qps peak, latency SLOs ~200ms p50 for short answers), our recommended path is: start with Redwood Dedicated (US + EU pools) for predictable latency and region isolation during the MAP, then evaluate a Private deployment only if you need on-prem or stricter network segregation. Hosted is the fastest to stand up but will require careful routing policies for EU traffic and SC/contract work to satisfy procurement.

2) Proposed MAP milestones (we'll deliver a 1-page MAP and an ops runbook):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff + baseline metrics (sample workload ingestion)
- Week 2–3: Perf runs + canary in EU region (Dedicated pool); success = p95 < 450ms and <5% error rate
- Week 4–5: Security/controls review (SOC2 artifacts + KMS binding) + cost projection
- Week 6–8: Integration testing + SLA/pricing review -> close decision and contract signature

3) Risks: model quantization vs latency trade-offs; KV cache warm-up for longer sequences; procurement timing for SOC2 artifact review. We can provide an accelerated evaluation if Healix commits to a small Dedicated deposit.

I'll attach a draft MAP and SOC bundle to the shared Drive in the next message. Karthik / Rishi / Camila — adding you for technical/commercial details.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: MAP_Healix_Hosting_Options_v3.xlsx (draft), mutual_action_plan.docx (template)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial MAP and hosting considerations for POC

Julia — adding technical detail so you have clear criteria for the perf runs.

Suggested evaluation plan (technical):
- Baseline: run the exact sample set you used in the demo (we'll provide a small harness) to capture tail latency with cold and warmed KV cache.
- Canary configuration: Dedicated pool with 1x A100-equivalent node in EU-west and 1x in us-central, routing EU-origin traffic to EU pool.
- Batching / quantization plan: start with fp16 for parity with your model weights; if cost needs to drop we recommend int8 quantized variant (we'll validate quality on your test prompts).
- Success gates: p50 < 180ms, p95 < 420ms, throughput sustained at 100 qps for 10 minutes without queue growth.

Operational asks: provide a sample workload replay and an account of peak concurrency windows so we can size burst and autoscale settings. I'll own the perf runout and support hooks.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Julia — commercial note and proposed close timeline.

Pricing/commit proposal:

Timeline:
- 8-week MAP aligned to the milestones Priya listed. Contract paperwork (SOW + security addendum) estimated at 7–10 business days once we receive PO from Healix.

Priya / team — thanks for the thorough breakdown and the Drive materials. After reviewing internally with engineering and procurement, Healix is inclined to proceed with a Dedicated-first MAP (US + EU pools) with the following asks before we sign: 

1) Regional isolation confirmation: Dedicated pools must guarantee EU customers' inference data and logs remain in EU region (we need a short clause for this).
2) SOC2 artifacts: please share the focused SOC2 evidence packet and the controls matrix (we reviewed the extract but need the controls summary).
3) Canary window: we agree to the performance gates Karthik suggested; request a 2-week canary in EU with our traffic shape.

If Redwood can put those three pieces in the SOW and accept the 8-week MAP timeline, Healix will issue a PO for the pilot week after next.

On procurement timing: Ben will be point; Ben, please confirm preferred PO format and if you need a redlined SOW template.

Thanks — looking forward to the formal MAP.

Julia
